corrections: R1: candidate §6.4 full-rank example is misstated. For m active indices, each retained chain of sizes t+1,...,m has rank m-t; the two chains share the full row, so for m=2t combined rank is at most m-1. One added independent row only fills deficiency when t=1. Correct example: identity and reverse orders with m>=2t+1 and unit weights give full rank. Consecutive large prefix differences yield e_(t+2),...,e_m in first order and e_1,...,e_(m-t-1) in reverse; if m=2t+1 the remaining middle basis vector comes from total row, and if larger the ranges cover all coordinates. Hence simple keep-all-large-rows rounding can stall, but the report's threshold/example must not be reused.
